questions.question: Which of the following glands secretes growth hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pituitary gland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Growth hormone (GH)**, also called somatotropin, is secreted by the **pituitary gland**. It plays a crucial role in stimulating growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration in humans.
 
• The pituitary gland is located at the base of the brain, just beneath the hypothalamus. It is often referred to as the **"master gland"** because it controls the activity of other endocrine glands.
 
• The secretion of growth hormone is regulated by the hypothalamus through two hormones: **Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH)**, which stimulates its release, and **Somatostatin**, which inhibits its release. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• **Functions of Growth Hormone:** It promotes the growth of bones and tissues, enhances protein synthesis, stimulates fat metabolism, and increases blood glucose levels.
 
• Deficiency of growth hormone can lead to **dwarfism** in children, while excess secretion can cause **gigantism** in children or **acromegaly** in adults. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other glands and their functions:**

 
 
• **Ovaries:** Found in females, they produce **estrogen** and **progesterone**, which regulate the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and secondary sexual characteristics.
 
• **Testes:** Found in males, they secrete **testosterone**, which plays a vital role in the development of male reproductive organs and secondary sexual characteristics.
 
• **Thyroid gland:** Located in the neck, it secretes **thyroxine** and **triiodothyronine**, which regulate metabolism, energy production, and growth.
 
 
 
• **Pituitary gland:**
 
 
• Known as the **"master gland"**, it controls the secretion of hormones from other glands such as the thyroid, adrenal glands, and gonads.
 
• **Examples:** Apart from growth hormone, it also secretes hormones like **prolactin**, which stimulates milk production, and **adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)**, which stimulates the adrenal glands.
 
 
 
• **Regulation of Growth Hormone:**
 
 
• Its secretion increases during sleep, exercise, and stress, highlighting the importance of lifestyle factors in hormonal balance.
 
• **Medical application:** Synthetic growth hormone is used to treat growth hormone deficiencies and certain conditions like Turner syndrome.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disorders related to Growth Hormone:**

 
 
• **Dwarfism:** Caused by insufficient growth hormone during childhood. Results in shorter stature and delayed physical development.
 
• **Gigantism:** Excess secretion during childhood leads to abnormal height and larger body proportions.
 
• **Acromegaly:** Excess secretion in adulthood causes abnormal growth of bones in the face, hands, and feet.
 
 
 
• **Hormonal Balance:**
 
 
• Maintaining proper diet, exercise, and sleep is essential for optimal growth hormone secretion and overall health.

questions.question: If the radii of curvature of two spherical mirrors are 2X and 4Y (X and Y are distances), what is the ratio of their focal lengths?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**X/2Y**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **focal length (f)** of a spherical mirror is given by the formula: **f = R/2**, where **R** is the radius of curvature of the mirror.
 
• For the first mirror, the radius of curvature is **2X**. Therefore, the focal length of the first mirror is given by:

 **f₁ = R₁/2 = 2X/2 = X.**
 
• For the second mirror, the radius of curvature is **4Y**. Therefore, the focal length of the second mirror is given by:

 **f₂ = R₂/2 = 4Y/2 = 2Y.**
 
• Now, the ratio of their focal lengths can be calculated as:

 **f₁ : f₂ = X : 2Y = X/2Y.**
 
• Hence, the ratio of the focal lengths of the two mirrors is **X/2Y**. *Therefore, the correct answer is X/2Y.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Spherical Mirrors:**

 
 
• Spherical mirrors are of two types: **concave mirrors** and **convex mirrors**.
 
• The **concave mirror** is curved inward (like a cave) and can converge light rays to a point.
 
• The **convex mirror** is curved outward and diverges light rays.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):**
 
 
• The radius of curvature is the distance between the center of curvature (C) and the mirror's surface.
 
• It is related to the focal length of the mirror by the formula **f = R/2**.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):**
 
 
• The focal length of a mirror is the distance between its focal point and the pole of the mirror.
 
• It determines how strongly the mirror converges or diverges light.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Concave mirrors** are used in telescopes, flashlights, and shaving mirrors because they concentrate light at a point.
 
• **Convex mirrors** are used in vehicles' rearview mirrors for a wider field of view.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:**

 
 
• The mirror formula is given as **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where:

 
 
• **f** is the focal length,
 
• **v** is the image distance,
 
• **u** is the object distance.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention:**
 
 
• In the case of spherical mirrors, distances are measured from the pole of the mirror.
 
• Distances measured along the direction of the incident light are taken as **positive**, while those measured in the opposite direction are taken as **negative**.
 
• For concave mirrors, the focal length is **negative**, and for convex mirrors, it is **positive**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• In optical instruments like microscopes and telescopes, the knowledge of focal length and radius of curvature is crucial for designing lenses and mirrors.
 
• Automotive industries use convex mirrors to provide a wider field of view for drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following tissue is responsible for movement in our body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscle tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muscle tissue** is the primary tissue responsible for movement in the human body. It is specialized to contract and produce motion in response to nervous system signals.
 
• Muscle tissue is composed of cells known as **muscle fibers** that contain contractile proteins like actin and myosin, enabling the generation of force and movement.
 
• There are three main types of muscle tissues: **skeletal muscle, smooth muscle, and cardiac muscle**. Each has a distinct structure and function.
 
• **Skeletal muscle:** It is responsible for voluntary movements, such as walking, running, and lifting objects. These muscles are attached to bones by tendons.
 
• **Smooth muscle:** Found in the walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels. It is responsible for involuntary movements like digestion and blood flow regulation.
 
• **Cardiac muscle:** Found exclusively in the heart, it is responsible for pumping blood throughout the body. It works involuntarily and continuously.
 
• Muscle tissue works in coordination with the **nervous system** to ensure proper movement and functioning of the body. *Hence, muscle tissue is responsible for movement in the body.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nervous Tissue:**

 
 
• **Nervous tissue** is responsible for transmitting signals between different parts of the body and coordinating bodily functions. It consists of neurons and glial cells.
 
• Though it plays a role in initiating and controlling movement by sending signals to muscle tissue, it is not directly responsible for the physical act of movement.
 
 
 
• **Connective Tissue:**
 
 
• **Connective tissue** supports, binds, and protects other tissues and organs. Examples include bones, tendons, and cartilage.
 
• It indirectly aids movement by serving as a framework for muscle attachment, but it does not produce movement itself.
 
 
 
• **Epithelial Tissue:**
 
 
• This type of tissue forms the outer covering of the body and lines internal organs and cavities. It provides protection and facilitates absorption, secretion, and filtration.
 
• Epithelial tissue is not involved in movement but instead acts as a protective barrier.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Muscle Tissue Characteristics:**

 
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are striated and voluntary, meaning they are under conscious control.
 
• **Smooth muscles** are non-striated and involuntary, functioning in processes like digestion and blood flow.
 
• **Cardiac muscle** is striated and involuntary, uniquely adapted for continuous contraction to pump blood.
 
 
 
• **Muscle Tissue Functions:**
 
 
• Facilitates locomotion and movement.
 
• Maintains posture and body position.
 
• Generates heat during contraction to maintain body temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about sensitivity in plants is INCORRECT?

options.text: Chemotropism is the growth response of plants to chemicals stimuli in their environment.
Thigmotropism is the response of plants to touch or physical contact.
Plants exhibit phototropism by growing towards the light source.
Plants have specialized Nervous tissues for conducting information.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants have specialized Nervous tissues for conducting information.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chemotropism:** This refers to the growth response of plants to a **chemical stimulus** in their environment. For instance, the growth of a pollen tube towards the ovule is guided by chemical signals. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Thigmotropism:** It is the response of plants to **touch or physical contact**. For example, the tendrils of a climbing plant wrap around a support when they touch it. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Phototropism:** Plants exhibit phototropism by growing towards a **light source**. This is typically observed in shoots, which grow towards light to maximize photosynthesis. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Specialized Nervous Tissues:** Unlike animals, plants do not have **specialized nervous tissues** for conducting information. Instead, they rely on chemical signaling and hormonal responses like auxins, cytokinins, and gibberellins to coordinate growth and responses to stimuli. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Plants have specialized Nervous tissues for conducting information.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tropisms in Plants:**

 
 
• **Chemotropism:** This is a directional growth movement of a plant in response to a chemical stimulus. It plays a critical role in reproduction, such as the growth of pollen tubes towards ovules for fertilization.
 
• **Thigmotropism:** Plants respond to mechanical stimuli like touch. For example, the tendrils of climbing plants curl around supports for stability and to grow upwards efficiently.
 
• **Phototropism:** Light is a crucial environmental stimulus for plants. Shoots exhibit **positive phototropism** (growth towards light), while roots often show **negative phototropism** (growth away from light).
 
 
 
• **Plant Signaling Mechanisms:**
 
 
• **Hormones:** Plants use chemical messengers like auxins, cytokinins, gibberellins, abscisic acid, and ethylene to regulate growth, development, and responses to environmental stimuli.
 
• **Electrical Signals:** Some plants, like the sensitive plant (*Mimosa pudica*), exhibit rapid movements due to electrical signaling, but they do not have a nervous system like animals.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Animals:**
 
 
• **Specialized Nervous System:** Unlike animals, plants lack a nervous system. Instead, they rely on slow chemical signaling to transmit information.
 
• **Adaptations:** Plants have evolved various tropic and nastic movements to adapt to their environments and respond effectively to stimuli.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Communication:** Plants use chemical signals like volatile organic compounds to communicate with other plants and attract pollinators or repel herbivores.
 
• **Auxins:** Auxins are plant hormones that regulate cell elongation and are key to phototropism and gravitropism.
 
• **Adaptation to Stimuli:** Tropic movements in plants help them optimize resources like light, water, and nutrients to survive in diverse environments.

questions.question: ________ light produces a spectrum similar to sunlight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**White**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **White light** is composed of all the colors of the visible spectrum. When passed through a prism, it splits into its constituent colors, forming a spectrum similar to sunlight.
 
• Sunlight is essentially white light and consists of a balanced combination of various wavelengths ranging from violet to red. *Hence, white light produces a spectrum similar to sunlight.*
 
• Artificial sources of light, such as LED bulbs designed to emit **white light**, mimic the spectral distribution of sunlight, making them ideal for environments requiring natural lighting conditions.
 
• Other colors, such as **yellow, blue, or other monochromatic lights**, do not produce the full spectrum similar to sunlight. These colors represent specific wavelengths and lack the balanced distribution of all colors. *Hence, options like yellow and blue do not fulfill the condition.*
 
• White light is widely used in applications such as photography, interior lighting, and optical studies because of its resemblance to natural sunlight. *Hence, the correct answer is white.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of White Light:**

 
 
• **White light** is formed by combining all wavelengths of the visible spectrum, including **red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet**. It is also referred to as polychromatic light.
 
• **Natural sunlight** acts as a perfect example of white light. When sunlight passes through a prism, it forms a rainbow-like spectrum, representing its full wavelength range.
 
 
 
• **Uses and Applications:**
 
 
• White light is extensively used in **scientific studies, optical experiments, and spectroscopy** due to its ability to split into all constituent colors.
 
• It is a preferred choice for **daylight-mimicking LED lights**, which are used in homes, offices, and photography studios.
 
• **Example:** White light is employed in **medical imaging devices and projectors** to ensure accurate reproduction of colors.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Colors:**
 
 
• **Yellow light:** Emits a single wavelength and is primarily used in streetlights but does not produce a full spectrum.
 
• **Blue light:** Consists of a shorter wavelength, often used in screens and electronic devices, but lacks the balanced spectral distribution similar to sunlight.
 
• **White light:** Combines all wavelengths and mimics sunlight, making it ideal for environments requiring natural illumination.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Basis of White Light:**

 
 
• White light is formed when light waves of all visible frequencies combine. It is considered the complete light spectrum visible to the human eye.
 
• When passed through a prism or diffraction grating, white light splits into its constituent colors due to differences in wavelength and refraction.
 
 
 
• **Practical Implications:**
 
 
• **Lighting:** White light is used in environments requiring natural sunlight imitation, such as indoor spaces and greenhouses.
 
• **Scientific Experiments:** White light is utilized in spectroscopy for analyzing materials and understanding their properties.
 
• **Photography:** White light is essential for capturing accurate colors in images.

questions.question: Why do the hydrophobic tails of soap molecules stay inside the micelles?

options.text: They are strongly attracted to water.
They form chemical bonds with water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are repelled by water.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soap molecules** consist of two parts: a **hydrophilic head** (water-attracting) and a **hydrophobic tail** (water-repelling).
 
• When soap is added to water, the hydrophobic tails avoid contact with water due to their **non-polar nature**. Water is polar, and it does not interact favorably with non-polar substances. *Hence, the hydrophobic tails are repelled by water.*
 
• To minimize contact with water, the hydrophobic tails congregate inward, forming a spherical structure called a **micelle**. The hydrophilic heads face outward, interacting with water. *This is why micelles are formed.*
 
• The micelle structure is essential for soap’s cleaning action. The hydrophobic tails trap **oils, grease, and dirt**, which are insoluble in water, while the hydrophilic heads allow the micelles to remain suspended in water. *This mechanism explains soap's ability to clean surfaces effectively.*
 
• The statement "They are repelled by water" is correct as the hydrophobic tails do not dissolve or bond with water. Instead, they avoid water and arrange themselves inwards within the micelle. *Hence, the correct answer is validated.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Soap Molecules:**

 
 
• Soap molecules consist of a **hydrophilic head**, which is attracted to water, and a **hydrophobic tail**, which repels water. This dual nature is crucial for forming micelles in water.
 
• The hydrophilic head is typically composed of an ionic group like **carboxylate (-COO-)**, making it soluble in water, while the hydrophobic tail is a long chain of hydrocarbons, which avoids water.
 
 
 
• **Micelle Formation:**
 
 
• Micelles are spherical structures formed when soap is added to water. The hydrophilic heads face outward toward water, and the hydrophobic tails cluster inward, away from water.
 
• This arrangement minimizes the interaction between water and the hydrophobic tails, while allowing the hydrophilic heads to interact with the surrounding water molecules.
 
• **Example:** Micelles trap non-polar substances like **oil and grease**, allowing them to be rinsed away in water.
 
 
 
• **Soap Cleaning Mechanism:**
 
 
• Soap cleans by trapping dirt, oil, and grease within the hydrophobic tails of micelles, which are suspended in water due to the hydrophilic heads.
 
• The micelles surround and isolate the dirt particles, which can then be rinsed away with water, leaving the surface clean.
 
• **Applications:** Soap is used extensively in **personal hygiene, cleaning surfaces, and industrial processes** due to its ability to dissolve oils and remove dirt.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydrophobic and Hydrophilic Interactions:**

 
 
• Hydrophobic tails avoid water due to the **non-polar nature** of hydrocarbons, while hydrophilic heads interact with water due to their **polar nature**.
 
• This dual behavior leads to the formation of micelles, enabling soap to clean greasy and oily substances effectively.
 
 
 
• **Role of Micelles in Cleaning:**
 
 
• Micelles trap dirt and grease within the hydrophobic core, isolating them from water, and making them easy to wash away.
 
• This mechanism is essential for **soap's functionality** in cleaning processes, including washing clothes, utensils, and personal hygiene.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions would result in the fastest evaporation of water from an open container

options.text: Low humidity, high temperature and moving air
High humidity, low temperature and still air
Low humidity, low temperature and moving air
High humidity, high temperature and still air

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low humidity, high temperature, and moving air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Evaporation is the process through which liquid water changes into water vapor. It is influenced by factors such as **humidity, temperature, and air movement**.
 
• When **humidity** is low, the surrounding air has a reduced amount of water vapor, allowing more water molecules from the container to escape into the air. *Hence, low humidity enhances evaporation.*
 
• A **high temperature** increases the kinetic energy of water molecules, making them more likely to escape the liquid phase and become vapor. *Thus, high temperature boosts evaporation.*
 
• **Moving air** facilitates evaporation by continuously replacing the saturated air near the water surface with drier air. This helps maintain a high evaporation rate by removing water vapor. *Hence, moving air accelerates evaporation.*
 
• In contrast, **high humidity** and **still air** create an environment where the air is already saturated with water vapor, reducing the potential for evaporation. Similarly, **low temperature** decreases the energy available for water molecules to evaporate. *Thus, these conditions slow down evaporation.*
 
• The combination of **low humidity, high temperature, and moving air** provides the most favorable conditions for the fastest evaporation, as all three factors work together to facilitate the process. *Hence, the correct answer is "Low humidity, high temperature, and moving air".*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**

 
 
• **Humidity:** High humidity slows evaporation as the air is already saturated with water vapor. Low humidity accelerates evaporation by allowing more water molecules to escape into the atmosphere.
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures increase the kinetic energy of water molecules, enabling them to overcome intermolecular forces and evaporate faster.
 
• **Air Movement:** Moving air replaces saturated air near the water's surface with drier air, maintaining a gradient that promotes evaporation.
 
 
 
• **Real-World Examples:**
 
 
• Clothes dry faster on a sunny, windy day due to the combination of **high temperature, low humidity, and moving air.**
 
• Evaporation rates are higher in arid regions where **humidity** is naturally low.
 
• Industrial cooling towers use **forced air** to enhance evaporation and improve cooling efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Evaporation:**
 
 
• Evaporation is used in processes like **distillation**, where liquids are separated based on their boiling points.
 
• In agriculture, **evapotranspiration** helps estimate water needs for crops based on evaporation rates.
 
• Evaporation plays a crucial role in water cycle processes such as cloud formation and precipitation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evaporation in Daily Life:**

 
 
• Sweat evaporates faster in hot and windy conditions, helping regulate body temperature.
 
• Evaporation is the principle behind cooling mechanisms in air conditioners and refrigerators.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Understanding:**
 
 
• The rate of evaporation depends on the **vapor pressure** of water, which increases with temperature.
 
• Water's **boiling point** is the temperature at which vapor pressure equals atmospheric pressure, resulting in rapid evaporation.

questions.question: Which of the following factors in some reptiles can change the sex of developing eggs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD)** is a phenomenon in which the temperature of the environment during the incubation period of eggs determines the sex of the offspring.
 
• TSD is commonly observed in certain reptiles, such as **turtles, crocodiles, and some species of lizards**. In these species, genetic factors do not directly determine the sex of an individual.
 
• The temperature at which the eggs are incubated influences whether the embryos develop as **males or females**. For example:
 
 
• In some species, **lower temperatures** result in males, while **higher temperatures** result in females.
 
• In other species, the relationship may be reversed or more complex, with males produced at intermediate temperatures and females at both extremes.
 
 
 
• TSD is an adaptation that allows reptiles to respond to environmental conditions, potentially optimizing the survival and reproductive success of the population. *Hence, temperature is the correct factor influencing the sex of developing eggs in reptiles.*
 
• The other options, such as water, wind, and pressure, do not directly influence the sex determination process in reptiles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Temperature-Dependent Sex Determination (TSD):**

 
 
• TSD is classified into three main patterns:
 
 
• **Type Ia:** Males are produced at lower temperatures, and females are produced at higher temperatures (e.g., many turtles).
 
• **Type Ib:** Females are produced at lower temperatures, and males are produced at higher temperatures (e.g., some lizards).

questions.question: The Sun is visible ________ before actual sunrise due to atmospheric refraction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 minutes.**__

__
 
• **Atmospheric refraction** is the phenomenon where light rays bend as they pass through the Earth’s atmosphere due to varying densities and temperatures of atmospheric layers. This bending causes the Sun to appear slightly above its actual position.
 
• The Sun is visible **approximately 2 minutes before the actual sunrise** due to atmospheric refraction. This is because the light from the Sun bends while traveling through the denser atmosphere near the horizon. *Hence, the correct answer is ***2 minutes.**
 
• During sunrise and sunset, the Sun's rays travel a longer path through the atmosphere, resulting in significant bending of light. This effect makes the Sun visible even when it is geometrically below the horizon.
 
• Atmospheric refraction also contributes to the visibility of celestial objects like stars and planets for a slightly longer duration after they set or before they rise.
 
• The bending of light due to atmospheric refraction is influenced by factors such as the Earth’s curvature, atmospheric density, and temperature gradients.
 
• This phenomenon is an essential concept in astronomy and navigation, as it affects the perceived positions of celestial objects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors affecting atmospheric refraction:**

 
 
• **Density of the atmosphere:** Higher atmospheric density near the Earth’s surface causes stronger refraction. This is why light bends more near the horizon.
 
• **Temperature gradient:** Variations in atmospheric temperature cause changes in air density, which influences the bending of light rays.
 
• **Earth's curvature:** The curved surface of the Earth also affects the angle at which sunlight enters the atmosphere, contributing to refraction.
 
 
 
• **Applications of atmospheric refraction:**
 
 
• Determining sunrise and sunset timings accurately for astronomical observations.
 
• Used in navigation and surveying to correct for positional errors caused by refraction.
 
• Explains phenomena like the apparent flattening of the Sun near the horizon during sunrise and sunset.
 
 
 
• **Other effects of atmospheric refraction:**
 
 
• **Twinkling of stars:** Stars appear to twinkle due to the continuous bending of their light as it passes through varying atmospheric layers.
 
• **Apparent position of stars:** Stars are observed at positions slightly different from their actual geometric positions due to atmospheric refraction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Numerical value:** The Sun is visible for **approximately 2 minutes** before the actual sunrise due to atmospheric refraction.
 
• **Global application:** This phenomenon is consistent worldwide and is a fundamental principle in astronomy and Earth sciences.
 
• **Real-life example:** During sunrise, the Sun appears above the horizon even when it is geometrically below it, helping determine accurate timings for various activities like prayer times in many cultures.

questions.question: For image formation by a concave mirror, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: An object placed at the focus form a highly diminished image.

The size of the image is enlarged when the object is placed at

infinity.
The nature of the image is real and erect when the object is at the centre of curvature.
At the centre of curvature, the size of the image is the same as the size of the object.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**At the centre of curvature, the size of the image is the same as the size of the object.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed at the **focus** of a concave mirror, the reflected rays become parallel and do not converge to form an image. Instead, the image is formed at infinity. The image is highly enlarged, not diminished. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• When an object is placed at infinity, the light rays converge at the focus to form a highly diminished, inverted, and real image. Therefore, the size of the image is not enlarged, but rather reduced. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The image formed at the center of curvature is real and inverted, not real and erect. The size of the image is the same as the size of the object in this case. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• When the object is placed at the **center of curvature**, the image is formed at the center of curvature itself. In this case, the size of the image is the **same as the size of the object**, and the nature of the image is real and inverted. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Properties of a Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a **converging mirror** because it reflects light rays inward to a single focal point.
 
• The focal point is located on the principal axis, and the distance between the mirror's pole and the focal point is called the **focal length**.
 
• Concave mirrors are used in applications like **reflecting telescopes, headlights, shaving mirrors**, and many scientific instruments due to their ability to converge light.
 
 
 
• **Rules of Image Formation in Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• If the object is placed at infinity, the image is formed at the focus (highly diminished, real, and inverted).
 
• If the object is beyond the center of curvature, the image forms between the focus and center (diminished, real, and inverted).
 
• If the object is at the center of curvature, the image is formed at the center of curvature (same size, real, and inverted).
 
• If the object is between the center of curvature and focus, the image is formed beyond the center of curvature (enlarged, real, and inverted).
 
• If the object is placed at the focus, the image is formed at infinity (highly enlarged, real, and inverted).
 
• If the object is placed between the focus and pole, the image is virtual, enlarged, and erect.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• Used in **reflecting telescopes** to gather and focus light from distant stars and galaxies.
 
• Used in **headlights of vehicles** to produce a parallel beam of light.
 
• Used in **dentistry** and shaving mirrors to provide magnified and clear images.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Factors to Remember:**

 
 
• The nature of the image formed by a concave mirror depends on the **position of the object** relative to the focal length and center of curvature.
 
• Concave mirrors are the only mirrors that can produce **real images** (inverted) as well as **virtual images** (erect).

questions.question: The image formed by a convex mirror is always _________.

options.text: inverted and of same size as the object
erect and of same size as the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**erect and diminished**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex mirror** is a diverging mirror that curves outward. It reflects light rays outward, meaning they appear to originate from a point behind the mirror.
 
• The image formed by a convex mirror is always **virtual**, as the reflected rays never actually meet but seem to converge when extended backward. *Hence, the image is not real.*
 
• The image formed is always **erect** because it appears upright relative to the object. This is a characteristic of convex mirrors.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce a **diminished** image, meaning the image size is smaller than the actual object size. This occurs regardless of the object's distance from the mirror.
 
• The position of the image is always behind the mirror, and it appears closer to the mirror as the object moves farther away.
 
• Convex mirrors are often used in vehicles as **rearview mirrors** because they provide a wider field of view, allowing drivers to see more area behind them.
 
• The other options are incorrect as a convex mirror *cannot produce an inverted image* and does not form an image of the same size as the object. The image is always diminished and upright. *Hence, the correct answer is erect and diminished.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Convex Mirrors:**

 
 
• **Convex mirrors** are diverging mirrors that reflect light outward. They are designed to provide a wide field of view, making them ideal for safety and surveillance purposes.
 
• The image formed by a convex mirror is always **virtual, erect, and diminished**. These characteristics are independent of the object's distance from the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• Convex mirrors are widely used as **rearview mirrors** in vehicles because they give a wider field of view and help drivers detect traffic from behind.
 
• They are also used in **security and surveillance** in shops, parking lots, and blind corners to monitor activities across a wide area.
 
 
 
• **Principles of Image Formation:**
 
 
• The laws of reflection govern the behavior of light rays on convex mirrors. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
 
• In convex mirrors, the reflected rays diverge, and the image appears to form behind the mirror when the rays are extended backward.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Concave Mirrors:**

 
 
• Unlike convex mirrors, **concave mirrors** can form both real and virtual images. The image can be magnified, inverted, or diminished depending on the object's position relative to the mirror's focal point.
 
• Convex mirrors are preferred for applications requiring a wide field of view, while concave mirrors are used in applications like telescopes, headlights, and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Real-Life Examples:**
 
 
• A common example of a convex mirror is the **side-view mirror** in cars. It often comes with the warning, "Objects in the mirror are closer than they appear," due to the diminished size of the image.
 
• Convex mirrors are also used in **road safety** at blind turns or intersections to provide visibility and reduce accidents.

questions.question: Which of the following tissues covers the lining of the mouth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Squamous epithelium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Squamous epithelium** is a type of epithelial tissue that lines the inner surfaces of the mouth. It is made up of flat and scale-like cells arranged in layers.
 
• This type of tissue is well-suited to areas exposed to friction, abrasion, and mechanical stress, such as the lining of the oral cavity.
 
• The squamous epithelium in the mouth is part of the mucosal lining, providing a protective layer against physical damage and microbial invasion. *Hence, the correct answer is Squamous epithelium.*
 
• It is further classified as **non-keratinized** or **keratinized**, depending on the location. Non-keratinized squamous epithelium is found in areas like the inner cheeks, while keratinized epithelium is present in regions like the gums and hard palate, which require more protection.
 
• The connective tissue, columnar epithelium, and cuboidal epithelium are not involved in forming the lining of the mouth. These tissues are found in other parts of the body and perform different functions. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Epithelial Tissues and Their Types:**

 
 
• **Squamous epithelium:** Found in areas prone to wear and tear like the mouth, esophagus, and skin. It provides protection and can be keratinized or non-keratinized.
 
• **Columnar epithelium:** Composed of tall, column-like cells. Found in the digestive tract and respiratory system, where it aids in absorption and secretion. For example, the lining of the stomach and intestines.
 
• **Cuboidal epithelium:** Made up of cube-shaped cells. It is found in glands, ducts, and the kidney tubules, where it is involved in secretion and absorption.
 
• **Connective tissue:** Provides structural and functional support to the body. It includes bone, blood, adipose tissue, and cartilage, but does not form the lining of the mouth.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Squamous Epithelium in the Mouth:**
 
 
• The primary function is **protection**. It shields the underlying tissues from mechanical damage, pathogens, and other harmful substances.
 
• It also plays a role in maintaining **moisture** in the oral cavity and facilitating the smooth movement of food during chewing and swallowing.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Keratinized and Non-Keratinized Squamous Epithelium:**
 
 
• **Keratinized:** Found in areas like the gums and hard palate, which are exposed to greater friction and require a tougher protective layer.
 
• **Non-Keratinized:** Found in the inner lining of the cheeks and lips, where there is less friction, providing flexibility and moisture retention.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Differences Between Keratinized and Non-Keratinized Epithelium:**

 
 
• Keratinized epithelium has a layer of keratin, a tough, protective protein, making it more resistant to damage. It is found in high-stress areas.
 
• Non-keratinized epithelium lacks this keratin layer, making it softer and more flexible. It is found in areas with lower mechanical stress.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Relevance:**
 
 
• Conditions like oral ulcers, infections, and cancers often involve the squamous epithelium of the mouth. Regular oral hygiene and early detection are essential for preventing complications.
 
• The study of epithelial tissue is crucial in understanding many diseases and developing treatments, especially in fields like dentistry and pathology.

questions.question: Which of the following options is true about carbon compound combustion?

options.text: Needs more oxygen for complete combustion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Needs more oxygen for complete combustion.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Combustion of carbon compounds refers to the chemical reaction where carbon-based substances react with **oxygen** to produce energy in the form of heat and light.
 
• Complete combustion occurs when there is a sufficient supply of **oxygen**. It produces **carbon dioxide** and **water**, along with releasing maximum energy. Hence, statement 4 is correct.
 
• Incomplete combustion takes place when there is insufficient **oxygen**, leading to the formation of **carbon monoxide** and soot instead of carbon dioxide. This can also result in lesser energy production. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• Carbon compounds burn only in the presence of **oxygen**. Without oxygen, the reaction cannot proceed, as oxygen is a key reactant in combustion. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• Water is a common product of combustion for most hydrocarbons. When hydrogen atoms in the compound react with oxygen, they form **water** (H₂O). Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Needs more oxygen for complete combustion.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Complete Combustion:**

 
 
• Occurs in the presence of an adequate supply of **oxygen**. It produces maximum energy along with **carbon dioxide** and **water** as by-products.
 
• Examples include burning of fuels such as **methane** (CH₄) or other hydrocarbons in well-ventilated spaces.
 
• Chemical equation: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + Energy.
 
 
 
• **Incomplete Combustion:**
 
 
• Occurs due to a lack of sufficient **oxygen**. It produces harmful substances such as **carbon monoxide** (CO) and **soot**.
 
• Chemical equation: CH₄ + O₂ → CO + H₂O + Energy.
 
• Incomplete combustion leads to pollution and is less energy-efficient compared to complete combustion.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Complete combustion** is commonly used in engines, power plants, and cooking applications for efficient energy utilization.
 
• **Incomplete combustion** is a major concern in poorly ventilated areas, leading to indoor air pollution and health risks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics:**

 
 
• **Carbon monoxide (CO):** A dangerous gas produced during incomplete combustion. It is colorless, odorless, and can cause health problems like poisoning.
 
• **Energy output:** Complete combustion provides higher energy efficiency compared to incomplete combustion.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• **Incomplete combustion:** Contributes to air pollution and global warming due to the release of CO and soot.
 
• **Complete combustion:** Although cleaner, it can still contribute to greenhouse gas emissions through the production of CO₂.

questions.question: A concave mirror with a focal length of f is cut into two equal halves along its principal axis. What will be the focal length of each half?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It remains f.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that curves inward, resembling a portion of a hollow sphere.
 
• The **focal length (f)** of a concave mirror is the distance between its pole (the center of the mirror) and its focal point (the point where light rays parallel to the principal axis converge).
 
 
 
• **
 
 
• When the concave mirror is cut into two equal halves along the principal axis, each half retains the same curvature as the original mirror.
 
• The focal length** of a mirror depends solely on the radius of curvature and not on the size of the mirror. Since the radius of curvature of each half remains unchanged, the focal length of each half also remains unchanged.
 
• Hence, the focal length of each half remains **f** (unchanged).
 
 
 
• **
 
 
• While the focal length of each half remains unchanged, the ability of each half to gather light reduces because the total reflective surface area is halved.
 
• This affects the brightness of the image but does not alter the focal length.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Focal Length Formula:**

 
 
• The focal length (**f**) of a concave mirror is related to its radius of curvature (**R**) by the formula: **f = R/2**.
 
• Since cutting the mirror along the principal axis does not change the radius of curvature, the focal length remains constant.
 
 
 
• **
 
 
• Concave mirrors are widely used in applications where light needs to be focused, such as:
 
 
• Telescope:** In reflecting telescopes, concave mirrors gather and focus light from distant celestial objects.
 
• **Headlights:** In car headlights, concave mirrors focus light into a beam for effective illumination.
 
• **Shaving Mirrors:** Concave mirrors provide magnified reflections and are used for precision tasks.
 
 
 
 
 
• **
 
 
• Convex Mirror:** A spherical mirror that bulges outward. It always forms virtual, upright, and diminished images.
 
• **Plane Mirror:** A flat mirror that forms virtual, upright, and same-sized images.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Differences Between Focal Length and Light-Gathering Capacity:**

 
 
• The **focal length** is a geometric property of the mirror and does not change when the mirror is cut.
 
• The **light-gathering capacity** depends on the reflective surface area. When the mirror is cut, this capacity is reduced due to the smaller area.
 
 
 
• 
 
 
• While each half of the mirror retains its focal length, the reduced surface area affects the intensity of the light focused. This is significant in applications requiring high light intensity.

questions.question: What is the work done in moving a charge of 10 C between two points with a potential difference of 14 V?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**140 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work Done Formula:** The work done in moving a charge between two points is calculated using the formula: *Work Done (W) = Charge (Q) × Potential Difference (V)*.
 
• In this case, the **charge (Q)** is **10 C**, and the **potential difference (V)** is **14 V**.
 
• Substituting the values: *W = 10 × 14 = 140 J.* Hence, the work done is **140 J**. *This calculation is correct.*
 
• ** The unit of work done is Joules (J**), which is derived as: *1 Joule = 1 Coulomb × 1 Volt.* This confirms the calculation.
 
• Moving a charge in an electric field involves work done proportional to the potential difference and the magnitude of the charge. *Hence, 140 J is the correct value.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Potential and Work:**

 
 
• **Electric potential** is the work done per unit charge to move a charge from one point to another in an electric field.
 
• The **potential difference** between two points in an electric field represents the amount of work required to move a unit charge between those points.
 
• Work is directly proportional to both the **charge (Q)** and the **potential difference (V)**.
 
 
 
• **Application of Work Done:**
 
 
• This principle is used in various applications, such as **batteries, capacitors, and electric circuits**, where energy transfer occurs due to movement of charges.
 
• In physics, work done in moving charges is fundamental to studying **electric fields**, **potential energy**, and **circuit behavior**.
 
 
 
• **Units and Measurement:**
 
 
• The unit of work is **Joule**, and the unit of potential difference is **Volt** (V).
 
• Charge is measured in **Coulombs**, denoted by the symbol **C**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Concepts in Electric Work:**

 
 
• **Potential difference:** This is a measure of the difference in electric potential between two points, and it drives the movement of charges in an electric field.
 
• **Work done:** It is an essential concept in energy transfer and the study of circuits, as it determines the energy required to perform electrical operations.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• The principle of work done is applied in **electric motors, generators, and energy storage devices**, which rely on the movement of charges.
 
• It is also fundamental in understanding the functioning of **batteries** and **electrical appliances**.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the reactivity series of metals. Which of these statements is/are correct?

**Statement I :** A piece of iron placed a solution of copper sulfate gradually develops a reddish layer.

**Statement II :** Copper is more reactive than iron and replaces it in the solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I:** A piece of iron placed in a solution of copper sulfate gradually develops a reddish layer.

 
 
• This is due to a chemical reaction where **iron displaces copper** from copper sulfate solution.
 
• Iron is **more reactive** than copper according to the reactivity series of metals, so it replaces copper in the compound.
 
• The reddish layer on the iron is due to the deposition of **copper metal** on the surface of the iron. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement II:** Copper is more reactive than iron and replaces it in the solution.
 
 
• This statement is **false**. Copper is **less reactive** than iron according to the reactivity series of metals.
 
• In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its solution. Since iron is more reactive than copper, it replaces copper in copper sulfate solution, not the other way around.
 
• *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• The reactivity series is an arrangement of metals in decreasing order of their reactivity. This series predicts how metals will react with solutions of other metals and helps explain the displacement reactions. Iron being more reactive than copper is key to this reaction.
 
• Therefore, ***Only Statement 1 is true**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of their decreasing reactivity.
 
• Metals like potassium, sodium, and calcium are highly reactive, while gold and platinum are very unreactive.
 
• In the series, **iron** is placed above **copper**, indicating that iron is more reactive than copper.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction:**
 
 
• A **displacement reaction** occurs when a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.
 
• For example, when a piece of iron is placed in copper sulfate solution, the reaction is:
 
Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu

 
 
• Iron displaces copper from the solution, forming iron sulfate and depositing copper metal.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Reactivity Series:**
 
 
• Used to predict metal displacement reactions.
 
• Helps in extraction of metals from their ores.
 
• Explains corrosion and methods to prevent it (e.g., galvanization).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reactivity of Metals:**

 
 
• Metals at the top of the reactivity series, such as potassium and sodium, react violently with water and acids.
 
• Metals at the bottom, such as gold and platinum, do not react with water or acids, making them ideal for use in jewelry.
 
 
 
• **Practical Implications:**
 
 
• Understanding the reactivity series helps in choosing suitable materials for construction and preventing corrosion.
 
• For example, zinc is used to galvanize iron because it is more reactive than iron and prevents its oxidation.

questions.question:
Pipe P can fill (2)/(3) of a tank in 20 hours, and pipe Q can fill (5)/(9) of the same tank in 25 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 3 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 4 hours.

**Question:** Pipes P, Q, and R together can fill the empty tank in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe P fills(2)/(3) part of the tank in 20 hours.

Pipe Q fills (5)/(9) part of the tank in 25 hours.

Pipes P and Q are open for 3 hours.

Pipe R empties the filled water in 4 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work / Time taken

Time to fill together = Total Work / Combined Efficiency

**Calculations:**

Time taken by P to fill = 20 × 3/2 = 30 hours.

Time taken by Q to fill = 25 × 9/5 = 45 hours.

Let the capacity of the tank (Total Work) be the LCM of 30 and 45.

LCM(30, 45) = 90 units (Total Capacity).

Efficiency of P = 90 / 30 = 3 units/hour (Filling).

Efficiency of Q = 90 / 45 = 2 units/hour (Filling).

Combined efficiency of P and Q= 3 + 2 = 5 units/hour.

**Water filled by P and Q in 3 hours:**

Water filled in 3 hours = {P+Q} × 3 hours

⇒ Water filled = 5 × 3 = 15 units.

**The efficiency of R :**

Pipe R empties the 15 units of water in 4 hours.

Efficiency of R = Water emptied / Time taken

⇒ R = 15 / 4 units/hour (Emptying).

**Time taken by P, Q, and R together to fill the empty tank:**

Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = P + Q - R

⇒ 3 + 2 - 15/4

⇒ 5/4 units/hour (Filling).

Time taken to fill the entire tank (90 units) = Total Capacity / Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 90 / (5/4)

⇒ Time = 90 × 4/5

⇒ Time = 18 × 4 = 72 hours.

**Therefore Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in 72 hours.**
